title: Choose the visual world for Hammerwell Piano Care
question: The roll assigned The Urtext Edition. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Urtext Edition
options.lineage: Plain-colour sheet-music edition covers and engraved scores
options.thesis: The practice is published like a scholarly music edition: a saturated cloth-colour cover, then engraved pages inside.
options.viewport: The whole viewport is the cover: an edition-blue field with a framed title cartouche (Hammerwell Piano Care / Tuning · Regulation · Repair), a catalogue number, and the booking form set inside the cartouche as the edition's contents.
options.risk: Can read as a music-shop catalogue if the cartouche is timid; the cover colour has to own the whole first viewport.

raised.raise: Total colour commitment: the cover blue fills the viewport edge to edge, no neutral ground behind it.
Empty states are drawn: unbooked visit days are empty staff bars, not missing cells.
Services are ranked by how often a piano needs them; type size carries the ranking.
One accent (gilt) marks only the current or selected state, nowhere else.
Every service carries its tag: how long it takes and what you get written down afterwards.

options.label: The Service Card
options.thesis: The page is the written card every visit ends with: pitch found, pitch left, what to watch.
options.viewport: A single oversized service card, filled in with a sample visit, with the booking form as a blank card underneath.
options.risk: It is the most obvious reading of this business's own mechanism, and the paper-card look is a common one.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Services set as two dense columns around a vermilion rail of keys, with technician notes hung in the margin.
options.viewport: A small text block of services in a wide margin, the rail of service keys down the centre, the booking form in the margin.
options.case: Its marginal notes suit 'technicians who explain', but it reads as a book, not a service you book.
options.risk: Bone paper plus serif is close to the default look AI pages ship.

options.label: Ebru Floated Pigment
options.viewport: A fluid bath across the viewport.
options.case: Piano owners don't recognise themselves in it, and it says nothing about tuning.
options.kept: Total colour commitment across the whole frame.

options.label: Seven-Segment Display
options.thesis: Every glyph from one eight-cell mask.
options.case: Cold for families and schools; reads as electronics, not craft.

options.label: Soundsystem Dance Poster
options.case: Wrong energy for someone trusting a stranger with an heirloom instrument.
options.kept: Ranking by weight, with type size as the ranking.

options.label: Rain-Night Cityscape
options.case: No link to pianos or home visits.
options.kept: One single marker for the current state.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Shadows traded with their stories attached.
options.case: Too strange for a practical booking.
options.kept: Every item carries its ticket of origin.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean local-service page: hero photo of a piano, services grid, testimonials, contact form.
canonCard.viewport: A photo of piano keys with a headline and a Book button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other piano tuner's site.
